target_customer: Satellite operators, constellation builders, and civil and defense launch customers needing orbital access
problem: Launch is expensive because rockets are only partly reusable. Stoke is building a fully and rapidly reusable two stage vehicle, Nova, to cut cost to orbit.

founders.name: Andy Lapsa
education: University of Michigan, PhD aerospace engineering
founders.background_notes: Per search summaries of GeekWire and Contrary Research (not opened in full): about a decade at Blue Origin on BE-3, BE-3U and BE-4 engines. Co-founder per YC page.

founders.name: Tom Feldman
education: Purdue University, BS and MS aerospace engineering
founders.background_notes: Per search summaries of Contrary Research and Wikipedia; designed BE-4 components. One source also mentions SpaceX, not confirmed. Co-founder per YC page.

competitors.name: SpaceX
competitors.what: Reusable Falcon 9 first stage; Starship in development as fully reusable

competitors.name: Rocket Lab
competitors.what: Small launch with Electron, booster recovery experiments

competitors.name: Relativity Space
competitors.what: 3D printed rockets, Terran R planned reusable

technical_complexity.rationale: Fully reusable rocket with novel regeneratively cooled heat shield and orbital engine; research-grade aerospace hardware for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Design know-how, launch licensing and pad access, and enormous capital needs make replication slow. SpaceX is the structurally stronger rival.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought Stoke; SpaceX pursued its own full reuse through Starship, and Stoke continued raising through 2026.

market_need_then: Satellite constellation demand and the success of reusable boosters showed launch demand and cost pressure at the time of the Winter 2021 batch.

branding.domain_note: Uses stokespace.com; acquisition history not found.
branding.brand_signature: Nova rocket name and 'Any Orbit. Any Time.'

rebrands.why: Company said the new name is stronger, more distinctive and reflects hardware DNA; this is the software platform, not the company.

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press attention on funding and hop tests; Gizmodo remarked on naming a rocket after a cataclysmic explosion.

brand_strength.rationale: Solid trade press and a clear rocket name, but not a consumer brand; brand matters mainly for hiring and investor attention.

outcome_analysis: Stoke has raised on a steady cadence from a 2021 seed through a reported 1B raise in September 2026, driven by founders with Blue Origin engine experience and a clear technical thesis of full reuse. It has not yet reached orbit, so the outcome rests on execution risk and capital needs rather than market need.
notes: Founder education and employer details come from search summaries of GeekWire, Contrary Research and Wikipedia; YC page lacks bios. Competitor list comes from a TechCrunch article on the Dec 2021 Series A as summarized by search, within about nine months after the batch; not opened directly. Series C date is Jan 2025 (URL 20250110; fetch said Jan 15). Series D 510M and 350M extension have no named investors in sources opened; the 1B Sept 2026 round is labeled Series E by other outlets and its leads come from a search summary. Valuation not stated anywhere. No layoffs, failures or acquisition found.
